experiment: FirstTrial v5 — calm-gap abstention and dead-ball error audit
scope: Exploratory scores on the public five-minute example; 7,500 graded frames and 17 ground-truth possession spells.
design: Seven fixed comparisons. V5 tests X on every missing-ball frame versus X only on calm missing-ball frames. No public answers are used to predict, fit, or select a model.

external_data_assessment.prohibited: Private full-match ground truth and other sources of corrected possession labels for the BAR-ATH fixture.
external_data_assessment.candidate: Metrica Sports public sample-data repository: three anonymized matches with synchronized tracking and event data.
external_data_assessment.reason_not_used: The local shell could not resolve GitHub to download the sample files.

interpretation: V5 abstention did not improve Spell F1. V2 remains the best measured public-sample Spell F1 method. V3 improves dead-ball recall but still misses over half of public D frames; the next experiment should prioritize live-versus-stopped detection. None of these scores establishes full-match performance.
limitations: The public sample contains only 17 possession spells and has already informed V1-V5 experiments; it is not independent validation.
Only 11.8% of the public window has missing ball coordinates, compared with about 43% across the full tactical tracking file.
The scramble proxy uses anonymous player-track speed and acceleration; it does not prove that a tackle, turnover, or stoppage occurred.
The V5 X variants inherit the D labels of their parent methods and do not address dead-ball recall.
No external Metrica sample data was used to train these models.
